requirements.text: Full proposals must be submitted by 5 p.m. at the submitting organization's local time.

requirements.text: Jurisdictional governments and non-lead participating organizations in active RII Track-1 and E-CORE awards are eligible to apply.
requirements.source_quote: The eligibility criteria were expanded to include jurisdictional governments and non-lead participating organizations in active RII Track-1 and E-CORE awards.

requirements.text: Proposers must have a Jurisdictional Science and Technology (S&T) Plan or an equivalent plan.
requirements.source_quote: Eligibility was expanded to include a Jurisdictional Science and Technology (S&T) Plan, or an equivalent plan.

requirements.text: Proposers must demonstrate expectations for building connections to a jurisdiction’s existing and future jurisdiction-wide research capacity building awards and the EPSCoR Jurisdiction/State Office.
requirements.source_quote: Guidance was added regarding the expectations for building connections to a jurisdiction’s existing and future jurisdiction-wide research capacity building awards, and EPSCoR Jurisdiction/State Office where present, hereafter referred to as “Jurisdiction/State Office”.

requirements.text: Proposers must notify the Jurisdiction Steering Committee of an E-CORE proposal submission.
requirements.source_quote: A requirement was added for notifying the Jurisdiction Steering Committee of an E-CORE proposal submission

requirements.text: Each collaborating organization must be represented by a PI, at least one co-PI, or other senior/key personnel.
requirements.source_quote: The requirement that each collaborating organization be represented by a PI or at least one co-PI was expanded to include other senior/key personnel.

requirements.text: Proposers may submit up to ten letters of collaboration.
requirements.source_quote: The number of letters of collaboration that proposers may submit was increased to ten (10) letters of collaboration.

requirements.text: Proposals must be submitted in accordance with the NSF Proposal & Award Policies & Procedures Guide (PAPPG) effective for the relevant due date.
requirements.source_quote: Any proposal submitted in response to this solicitation should be submitted in accordance with the *NSF Proposal & Award Policies & Procedures Guide* (PAPPG) that is in effect for the relevant due date to which the proposal is being submitted.

requirements.source_quote: Projects will also support the development and growth of new jurisdiction-wide connections,

requirements.source_quote: Based on the evidence-based and self-identified needs of a jurisdiction,

requirements.text: Proposals must request funding for a duration of four years.
requirements.source_quote: Funding requests must be for a duration of four (4) years

requirements.text: The maximum total budget for the initial four-year period is $10 million.
requirements.source_quote: with a maximum budget of $10 million total for the first four years

requirements.text: If applicable, the optional renewal project award has a maximum total budget of $8 million for an additional four years.
requirements.source_quote: and an optional renewal project award maximum budget of $8 million total for an additional four years

requirements.text: Proposals can only be submitted by accredited institutions of higher education operating a campus within the United States, its territories, or possessions on behalf of their faculty.
requirements.source_quote: Institutions of higher education (PhD- and non-PhD-granting) that are accredited and operate a campus within the United States, its territories, or possessions, may submit proposals on behalf of their faculty.

requirements.text: Distinct academic campuses within multi-campus systems can qualify as separate eligible institutions if they award their own degrees and have independent administrative structures, admissions policies, and alumni associations.
requirements.source_quote: Distinct academic campuses within multi-campus systems (e.g., campuses that award their own degrees and have independent administrative structures, admissions policies, and alumni associations) qualify as separate submission-eligible institutions.

requirements.text: If planning to submit through another entity's Sponsored Projects Office, contact NSF EPSCoR at least six weeks before submission to discuss eligibility.
requirements.source_quote: Campuses that plan to submit a proposal through the Sponsored Projects Office of other campuses or organizations should contact NSF EPSCoR to discuss eligibility as early as possible and at least six weeks before submitting such a proposal.

requirements.text: Non-profit, non-degree-granting domestic U.S. organizations can submit proposals if they have an independent, permanent administrative organization in the U.S. territories/possessions and hold 501(c)(3) tax status.
requirements.source_quote: Non-profit, non-degree-granting domestic U.S. organizations, acting on behalf of their employees, that include (but are not limited to) independent museums and science centers, observatories, research laboratories, professional societies, and similar organizations that are directly associated with the Nation’s research or educational activities. These organizations must have an independent, permanent administrative organization (e.g., an office of sponsored research) located in the United States, its territories, or possessions, and have 501(c)(3) tax status.

requirements.text: Jurisdictional/state governments or their agencies/commissions can submit proposals when coordinating efforts of multiple organizations within the jurisdiction.
requirements.source_quote: Jurisdictional/state governments, or agencies or commissions thereof, when coordinating efforts of multiple organizations within the jurisdiction.

requirements.text: Tribal Governments can submit proposals with federally recognized tribes or Indigenous communities not recognized by the 1994 Act.
requirements.source_quote: Tribal Governments with the governing body of any Indian or Alaska Native tribe, band, nation, pueblo, village, or community that the Secretary of the Interior acknowledges to exist as an Indian tribe under the Federally Recognized Indian Tribe List Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 479a, et seq.) or Indigenous communities that are not recognized by the Federally Recognized Indian Tribe List Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 479a, et seq.).

requirements.text: E-CORE proposals must be submitted by organizations within jurisdictions meeting EPSCoR eligibility criteria.
requirements.source_quote: E-CORE proposals may only be submitted by organizations within jurisdictions meeting the [EPSCoR eligibility criteria](https://new.nsf.gov/funding/initiatives/epscor/epscor-criteria-eligibility).

requirements.text: Organizations currently serving as the lead on an active E-CORE or RII Track-1 award that is not in its final year or under a no-cost extension cannot submit E-CORE proposals.
requirements.source_quote: E-CORE proposals may not be submitted by organizations that serve as the lead organization on an active E-CORE or RII Track-1 award unless that award is in its final year or under a no-cost extension and will not be renewed.

requirements.text: E-CORE submissions must be multi-organizational, involving a lead organization and additional collaborating partners.
requirements.source_quote: E-CORE submissions should be multi-organizational, with a lead organization and additional collaborating partner(s), which may include academic and non-academic organizations.

requirements.text: Collaborations must demonstrate building or developing cores within the jurisdiction and an interconnected jurisdiction-wide network linking research efforts to individuals in the ecosystem.
requirements.source_quote: Collaborations must be indicative of building or developing cores within the jurisdiction and an interconnected jurisdiction-wide network that is able to link research efforts to individuals in a jurisdiction’s research ecosystem.

requirements.text: Collaborations with non-EPSCoR jurisdictions are allowed but must include unfunded collaborators because funds may only be allocated for activities/personnel within an EPSCoR jurisdiction.
requirements.source_quote: However, since EPSCoR program funds may only be allocated for activities and personnel within an EPSCoR jurisdiction, participation of collaborators in non-EPSCoR jurisdictions must be unfunded collaborators.

requirements.text: Principal Investigators must hold at least 50% appointments in eligible organizations within an EPSCoR jurisdiction.
requirements.source_quote: Principal Investigators must hold at least 50% appointments in eligible organizations within an EPSCoR jurisdiction.

requirements.text: Each collaborating organization must be represented by a PI, co-PI, or other senior/key personnel.
requirements.source_quote: Each collaborating organization must be represented by a PI, co-PI, or other senior/key personnel.

requirements.text: An organization may serve as the lead on only one RII Track-1 award, E-CORE submission, or E-CORE award at a time (with exceptions for final year/no-cost extension awards).
requirements.source_quote: An organization may serve as the lead on only one RII Track-1 award, E-CORE submission, or E-CORE award at a time, except when the active RII Track-1 or E-CORE award is in its final year or under a no-cost extension and will not be renewed.

requirements.text: Full proposals submitted via Research.gov must follow the guidelines in the NSF Proposal and Award Policies and Procedures Guide (PAPPG).
requirements.source_quote: Full Proposals submitted via Research.gov: *NSF Proposal and Award Policies and Procedures Guide* (PAPPG) guidelines apply.

requirements.text: Full proposals submitted via Grants.gov must follow the guidelines in the NSF Grants.gov Application Guide.
requirements.source_quote: Full Proposals submitted via Grants.gov: *NSF Grants.gov Application Guide: A Guide for the Preparation and Submission of NSF Applications via Grants.gov* guidelines apply

requirements.text: Voluntary committed cost sharing is not allowed.
requirements.source_quote: Inclusion of voluntary committed cost sharing is prohibited.

requirements.source_quote: the program will also support the development and growth of new jurisdiction-wide networks, and the leveraging of existing jurisdictional networks,

requirements.text: Projects must support the sustainability of research infrastructure cores beyond the award period using non-EPSCoR RII funds.
requirements.source_quote: E-CORE projects must be designed to support the sustainability of the research infrastructure cores beyond the award period with non-EPSCoR RII funds.

requirements.text: Proposals must establish a time-bound vision for enhancing R&D competitiveness with intentional involvement of emerging research institutions, minority-serving institutions, and other contributors.
requirements.source_quote: E-CORE proposals should establish a time-bound vision for how project activities will substantively and sustainably enhance the R&D competitiveness of a jurisdiction's organizations, with the intentional involvement of emerging research institutions, minority-serving institutions, and other important contributors to a jurisdiction's research ecosystem.

requirements.text: Proposers must describe opportunities to re-evaluate and evolve the vision and core activities as ecosystem needs evolve.
requirements.source_quote: To ensure sustainability, proposers should describe opportunities to re-evaluate and evolve the vision and core activities as the needs of the jurisdiction’s research ecosystem evolve.

requirements.text: Proposals must detail alignment with all five EPSCoR program goals.
requirements.source_quote: E-CORE proposals must also detail the alignment of the project with all five EPSCoR program goals.

requirements.text: Core selection must be justified by leveraging an assessment of jurisdiction needs, challenges, opportunities, team strengths, and priorities.
requirements.source_quote: A project’s cores should be identified and justified by leveraging an assessment of a jurisdiction’s needs, challenges, and opportunities, the strengths of the proposing team, and the jurisdiction’s priorities.

requirements.text: Justification for core selection must include a data-driven or evidence-based vision and assessment of identified needs and priorities.
requirements.source_quote: The proposal’s justification for core selection should include a data-driven or evidence-based vision and assessment of the identified needs and priorities of a jurisdiction.

requirements.text: Each project must have an Administrative Core that establishes a foundational framework connecting investigators and partners.
requirements.source_quote: Each E-CORE project must have an Administrative Core. A critical role of this core is to establish a foundational framework that connects groups of investigators and partners across the jurisdiction.

requirements.text: The Administrative Core must serve as the center of project management and include a Project Administrator or Manager.
requirements.source_quote: The Administrative Core should also serve as the center of project management for the E-CORE project and should include an individual serving in a role such as Project Administrator or Project Manager.

requirements.text: Proposers must provide a plan describing prior coordination efforts, how activities will be coordinated across the jurisdiction, and connections to other relevant NSF-funded capacity building awards.
requirements.source_quote: Proposers should provide a plan that describes the project’s prior coordination efforts in the jurisdiction, how project activities will be coordinated across the jurisdiction, and/or how connections will be made with the other projects mentioned above that seek to create jurisdiction-wide networks that build research capacity.

requirements.text: Proposals must put forth a clear plan for coordinating the Administrative Core with other E-CORE/EPSCoR projects and active Jurisdiction/State Offices.
requirements.source_quote: E-CORE proposals should put forth a clear plan of how the Administrative Core will coordinate with other present and future E-CORE and other types of EPSCoR and non-EPSCoR capacity building projects, with an active Jurisdiction/State Office (if present), and describe how they will coordinate with other federally funded projects that build capacity for substantive jurisdiction-wide research infrastructure.

requirements.text: Additional cores must be supported by a justifiable, evidence-based rationale including statistical or demographic data.
requirements.source_quote: The proposal should provide a justifiable and evidence-based rationale that includes statistical data, demographic data describing populations, or other types of data, for the selection of the additional core(s).

requirements.text: Proposals must focus on depth rather than breadth, selecting a limited number of cores relevant to the scope and budget.
requirements.source_quote: E-CORE projects should focus on depth rather than breadth in their selection of cores. An E-CORE project should include a limited number of cores relevant to the proposed scope of work and consistent with the budget request.

requirements.text: Selection of cores must be based on evidence-based analysis illustrating the need within the jurisdiction.
requirements.source_quote: The selection of a core must be based on evidence-based analysis that illustrates the need for that core within the jurisdiction.

requirements.text: Projects must operationalize five design elements: Jurisdictional Development, Research Ecosystem-Wide Connections, Broadening Participation/Reciprocal Collaboration, Goals/Metrics/Evaluation, and Intentional Communication.
requirements.source_quote: To build and support research networks to connect core activities within the jurisdiction, E-CORE projects must operationalize the following five design elements of collaborative infrastructure in ways that catalyze and accelerate systemic change and lead to substantially broadened participation in STEM research capacity:

requirements.text: Proposers must clearly articulate their contribution to the ecosystem, identify the addressed aspect, and demonstrate jurisdiction-wide impact.
requirements.source_quote: 1. Jurisdictional Development: Proposers must clearly articulate their contribution to the jurisdiction’s research ecosystem, identify what aspect of the ecosystem is being addressed, and demonstrate how the project will create jurisdiction-wide impact.

requirements.text: There must be a plan to gather participant feedback to assess progress and adjust broadening participation efforts.
requirements.source_quote: There should be a plan to gather feedback from participants that allows the project leadership to assess its progress and adjust as needed to continuously improve broadening participation efforts.

requirements.text: Projects must build collaborative infrastructure involving a broad array of individuals, communities, organizations, or Tribal Nations.
requirements.source_quote: E-CORE projects should build collaborative infrastructure (policies, processes, and procedures) throughout the project that involves a broad array of individuals, communities, organization types, or Tribal Nations.

requirements.text: The vision for reciprocal collaboration must include descriptions of the integration and roles of all partners.
requirements.source_quote: The vision for creating a culture of reciprocal collaboration should include descriptions of the integration and roles of all partners in the project.

requirements.text: Proposals must include a logic model or theory of change with measurable goals and objectives aligned with jurisdictional needs.
requirements.source_quote: 4. Goals, Metrics, and Evaluation: Proposals must include a logic model or theory of change that includes measurable goals and objectives aligned with jurisdictional needs, illustrating how the project’s research capacity and infrastructure will enhance the jurisdiction’s research ecosystem.

requirements.text: Projects must establish internal and external communication plans detailing recruitment, retention, visibility, and engagement strategies.
requirements.source_quote: 5. Intentional Communication: Projects must establish internal and external communication plans detailing strategies for recruiting and retaining participants. These plans should also outline efforts to promote project visibility and encourage active engagement from key partners.

requirements.text: Each project must include an evaluator to assess progress toward all elements of the project.
requirements.source_quote: Additionally, proposals must include a preliminary timetable or Gantt chart for achieving those goals. It is strongly recommended that proposals include a logic model with a clearly articulated theory of change that identifies appropriate indicators of progress toward the desired outcomes.

requirements.text: Proposals must include a preliminary timetable or Gantt chart for achieving goals.
requirements.source_quote: Additionally, proposals must include a preliminary timetable or Gantt chart for achieving those goals.

requirements.text: E-CORE proposals must include a plan for how the Administrative Core and other cores will interface with the Jurisdictional Steering Committee.
requirements.source_quote: E-CORE proposals must include a plan for how the Administrative Core (and other cores, if appropriate) will interface with the Jurisdictional Steering Committee.

requirements.text: For renewal project proposals, cost sharing is required at 20% of the total amount requested from NSF.
requirements.source_quote: Cost sharing for a renewal project proposal is required at the level of 20% of the total amount requested from NSF in the renewal project proposal’s budget.

requirements.text: E-CORE awards are initially made for four years, with an optional four-year renewal.
requirements.source_quote: Even though the award will be initially made for four years, with an optional four-year renewal project award, each year’s funding increment is dependent on progress towards the goals of the project.

requirements.text: Each year's funding increment is dependent on progress towards the goals of the project.

requirements.source_quote: Activities and products described by the strategic plan will be reported through the EPSCoR Data Outcomes Collection System (EDOCS).

requirements.source_quote: Up to $37,500,000 annually

requirements.source_quote: No-cost extensions may be granted only under rare and exceptional circumstances.

requirements.source_quote: Jurisdictional/state governments, or agencies or commissions thereof, when coordinating efforts of multiple organizations within the jurisdiction.

requirements.source_quote: List of Participating Organizations. Provide a list of all organizations (including, but not limited to, academic and research organizations, companies, government agencies, and non-profit organizations) that will participate in, contribute to, or directly benefit from the proposed project.

requirements.text: Letters of collaboration are allowed (up to ten, two pages each) to confirm commitments of resources.
requirements.source_quote: However, up to ten letters of collaboration (two pages or fewer) from partners or jurisdictional officials may be included to confirm commitments of resources beyond the core project investigators.

requirements.text: A copy of the jurisdiction’s S&T Plan (approved within the past five years) is required as a supplementary document.
requirements.source_quote: Submit a copy of the jurisdiction’s S&T Plan, or equivalent document, in the Other Supplementary Documents section. The plan must have been officially approved within the past five years by the Jurisdictional Steering Committee or a governing authority acting on behalf of the jurisdiction.

requirements.text: Evidence of official acceptance or approval of the S&T Plan (including effective date and signatures) must be indicated.
requirements.source_quote: Evidence of official acceptance or approval by the designated body or official, including the effective date and signature(s) of the approver(s), must be clearly indicated, either in the S&T Plan itself or via an official document (or letter) uploaded separately as a Supplementary Document.

requirements.text: A letter notifying the Jurisdictional Steering Committee (JSC) of the planned submission is required.
requirements.source_quote: Proposers should include in Supplementary Documentation a letter that the JSC has been notified about the upcoming submission of the proposal.

requirements.text: Voluntary committed cost sharing is not allowed for new E-CORE awards.
requirements.source_quote: Inclusion of voluntary committed cost sharing is prohibited.

requirements.text: Funding requests must be for a duration of four years with a maximum total budget of $10 million, though there is no restriction on the annual amount requested.
requirements.source_quote: Funding requests must be for a duration of four (4) years, with a maximum budget of up to $10 million total. There is no restriction on the amount requested annually.

requirements.text: EPSCoR funding cannot be used to support participants from non-EPSCoR jurisdictions, excluding consultants.
requirements.source_quote: Outside of consultants, EPSCoR funding may not be used to support participants from non-EPSCoR jurisdictions.

requirements.text: Subawards to organizations in non-EPSCoR jurisdictions are not permitted.
requirements.source_quote: Subawards to organizations in non-EPSCoR jurisdictions are not permitted since EPSCoR funds may not be allocated to organizations in non-EPSCoR jurisdictions.

requirements.text: Financial compensation for the independent evaluator(s) and strategic planning facilitator must be included in the submitting organization's budget under line G.3.
requirements.source_quote: Financial compensation for the independent evaluator(s) and a strategic planning facilitator must be included in the budget of the submitting organization under NSF budget line G.3 (Consultant Services).

requirements.text: Only the submitting organization's budget may include subawards; subawardee budgets cannot list subawards.
requirements.source_quote: Only the budget of the submitting organization may include subawards (i.e., no subawards may appear in the budgets of subawardee organizations).

requirements.text: For collaborative proposals from one organization, participating organization budgets must be included as subawards with a separate budget justification of no more than five pages.
requirements.source_quote: If the proposal is being submitted as a "Submission of a collaborative proposal from one organization," budgets for participating organizations must be included as subawards to the budget of the submitting organization. Each subaward must include a separate budget justification of no more than five pages (see PAPPG Chapter II.D.2.f).

requirements.text: For collaborative proposals from multiple organizations, proposers must follow PAPPG Chapter II.E.3 regarding budget submissions.
requirements.source_quote: If the proposal is being submitted as a "Submission of a collaborative proposal from multiple organizations," follow the instructions in PAPPG Chapter II.E.3 regarding budget submissions.

requirements.text: Budgets must comply with 2 CFR 200 and current NSF PAPPG, ensuring all costs are allowable, allocable, reasonable, and necessary.
requirements.source_quote: Proposal budgets must comply with the guidance in 2 CFR 200 and the current NSF Proposal and Award Policies and Procedures Guide (PAPPG). Proposing entities are cautioned to ensure that all costs proposed are allowable (allocable, reasonable, and necessary), especially those costs associated with participants (Line F on the Proposal Budget).

requirements.text: Costs typically considered entertainment, amusement, or promotional must be justified in the budget justification if they are necessary for programmatic objectives like STEM enrichment or cohort-building.
requirements.source_quote: When costs typically considered as entertainment, amusement, and promotion are necessary to accomplish the proposed objectives, they must be included in the budget and justified in the budget justification.

requirements.text: Jurisdictions submitting budgets with subawards (Line G5) must verify that the lead organization has a system to monitor subawards and appropriate agreements are in place.
requirements.source_quote: Jurisdictions submitting proposal budgets with Subawards (Line G5 on the Proposal Budget) must be able to verify that the lead organization has established a system to monitor the subawards issued on Federally sponsored projects and that appropriate agreements are in place with subrecipients.

requirements.text: Cost sharing is required for E-CORE renewal project awards at least 20% of the total amount requested.
requirements.source_quote: Cost sharing for a renewal project award is required at the level of at least, and no more than, 20% of the total amount requested in the renewal project budget.

requirements.text: An explanation of the source, nature, amount, and availability of required cost sharing must be provided in the budget justification for renewal proposals.
requirements.source_quote: An explanation of the source, nature, amount, and availability of the required cost sharing must be provided in the budget justification of the Renewal Proposal (see PAPPG Chapter II.D.2.f.xii and Chapter VII.C)

requirements.text: For submissions after the initial date, proposals are due on the third Tuesday in July every year.
requirements.source_quote: Third Tuesday in July, Annually Thereafter

requirements.text: For proposals submitted via Grants.gov, they must pass all NSF pre-check and post-check validations to be accepted.
requirements.source_quote: Grants.gov proposals must pass all NSF pre-check and post-check validations in order to be accepted by Research.gov at NSF.

requirements.text: If a proposal fails post-checks after passing pre-checks, corrections must be made and resubmitted in Research.gov, not Grants.gov.
requirements.source_quote: Once a proposal passes pre-checks but fails any post-check, an applicant can only correct and submit the in-progress proposal in Research.gov.

requirements.text: Authorized Organizational Representatives submitting via Grants.gov must verify the desired funding opportunity and agency during submission.
requirements.source_quote: The AOR must then sign and submit the application to Grants.gov. The completed application will be transferred to Research.gov for further processing.

requirements.text: Organizations using Grants.gov must register first to create an institutional profile.
requirements.source_quote: Before using Grants.gov for the first time, each organization must register to create an institutional profile.

requirements.text: NSF strongly recommends initiating proposal submission via Grants.gov at least five business days before the deadline.
requirements.source_quote: When submitting via Grants.gov, NSF strongly recommends applicants initiate proposal submission at least five business days in advance of a deadline

requirements.text: The proposal must include clearly stated goals for Broader Impacts activities.
requirements.source_quote: individual projects should include clearly stated goals
requirements.source_heading: VI. NSF Proposal Processing And Review Procedures

requirements.text: The proposal must include specific descriptions of the activities the PI intends to do for Broader Impacts.
requirements.source_quote: specific descriptions of the activities that the PI intends to do
requirements.source_heading: VI. NSF Proposal Processing And Review Procedures

requirements.text: The proposal must include a plan to document the outputs of Broader Impacts activities.
requirements.source_quote: and a plan in place to document the outputs of those activities.
requirements.source_heading: VI. NSF Proposal Processing And Review Procedures

requirements.text: For the E-CORE competition, proposers must justify each core and demonstrate its potential to substantially benefit jurisdictional research capacity with evidence.
requirements.source_quote: Are all cores well justified to the needs of the jurisdiction? Is there the potential, based on evidence provided and/or referenced in the proposal, for each core to substantially benefit jurisdictional research capacity?
requirements.source_heading: VI. NSF Proposal Processing And Review Procedures

requirements.text: For the E-CORE competition, proposers must show that cores are aligned with EPSCoR mission and goals.
requirements.source_quote: Are the cores aligned to EPSCoR mission and goals?
requirements.source_heading: VI. NSF Proposal Processing And Review Procedures

requirements.text: For the E-CORE competition, proposers must describe a clear pathway to sustainability for the efforts.
requirements.source_quote: Are the efforts sustainable, with a clear pathway to sustainability?
requirements.source_heading: VI. NSF Proposal Processing And Review Procedures

requirements.text: For the E-CORE competition, proposers must explain how the project will coordinate with current or future E-CORE projects and/or other jurisdiction-wide capacity building efforts.
requirements.source_quote: Is there a clear description of how the project will coordinate with current or future E-CORE projects and/or other jurisdiction-wide capacity building efforts?
requirements.source_heading: VI. NSF Proposal Processing And Review Procedures

requirements.text: For the E-CORE competition, proposers must describe how the project embodies broadening participation throughout all activities as part of its jurisdiction-wide vision.
requirements.source_quote: How well does the proposal describe how the project and project leadership embodies broadening participation throughout all activities as part of its jurisdiction-wide vision?
requirements.source_heading: VI. NSF Proposal Processing And Review Procedures

requirements.text: For the E-CORE competition, proposers must describe the extent of broad participation by individuals and organizations integrated into project activities.
requirements.source_quote: To what extent is there a broad participation of individuals and organizations integrated into project activities?
requirements.source_heading: VI. NSF Proposal Processing And Review Procedures

requirements.text: For the E-CORE competition, proposers must provide a reasonable plan for forming a visionary and effective leadership team.
requirements.source_quote: Does the proposal provide a reasonable plan for forming a visionary and effective leadership team?
requirements.source_heading: VI. NSF Proposal Processing And Review Procedures

requirements.text: For the E-CORE competition, proposers must describe how necessary disciplines, skills, perspectives, and capabilities will be brought together.
requirements.source_quote: Does the proposal describe a well-informed process by which all necessary disciplines, skills, perspectives, and capabilities will be brought together to form an interdependent and multidisciplinary leadership team that can work and communicate effectively?
requirements.source_heading: VI. NSF Proposal Processing And Review Procedures

requirements.text: For the E-CORE competition, proposers must show that partners from multiple organizations are represented among the leadership team with a clear connection to the project.
requirements.source_quote: Are there partners from multiple organizations represented among the leadership team with a clear connection to the project?
requirements.source_heading: VI. NSF Proposal Processing And Review Procedures

requirements.text: For the E-CORE competition, proposers must provide evidence that each project element will be well executed and allow for meaningful engagement with the Jurisdictional Steering Committee.
requirements.source_quote: Do the execution plan and evaluation and assessment plan provide evidence that each project element will be well executed and will allow for clear and meaningful engagement with the Jurisdictional Steering Committee?
requirements.source_heading: VI. NSF Proposal Processing And Review Procedures

requirements.text: Proposals must be evaluated by reviewers using two National Science Board approved merit review criteria and any applicable program-specific criteria.
requirements.source_quote: Reviewers will be asked to evaluate proposals using two National Science Board approved merit review criteria and, if applicable, additional program specific criteria.

requirements.text: Principal Investigators or organizations must not make financial or personnel commitments for the project unless a grant is signed by an NSF Grants and Agreements Officer.
requirements.source_quote: A Principal Investigator or organization that makes financial or personnel commitments in the absence of a grant or cooperative agreement signed by the NSF Grants and Agreements Officer does so at their own risk.

requirements.text: The submitting organization will receive award notification from an NSF Grants and Agreements Officer.
requirements.source_quote: Notification of the award is made to *the submitting organization* by an NSF Grants and Agreements Officer.

requirements.text: Declined proposals will be notified as promptly as possible by the cognizant NSF Program.
requirements.source_quote: Organizations whose proposals are declined will be advised as promptly as possible by the cognizant NSF Program administering the program.

requirements.text: Verbatim copies of reviews, with reviewer identities removed, will be automatically provided to the Principal Investigator.
requirements.source_quote: Verbatim copies of reviews, not including the identity of the reviewer, will be provided automatically to the Principal Investigator.

requirements.text: If receiving funding for infrastructure projects, all iron, steel, manufactured products, and construction materials must be produced in the United States.
requirements.source_quote: no funding made available through this funding opportunity may be obligated for infrastructure projects under an award unless all iron, steel, manufactured products, and construction materials used in the project are produced in the United States.

requirements.text: E-CORE projects must partner with the Jurisdictional Steering Committee to assess and identify evolving strengths in the jurisdiction's research landscape.
requirements.source_quote: E-CORE projects are expected to partner with the Jurisdictional Steering Committee to continually assess and identify evolving strengths within the research landscape of the jurisdiction.

requirements.text: The assessments of evolving strengths must be data-driven and evidence-based to inform the update of the S&T plan.
requirements.source_quote: These assessments should be data-driven and evidence-based and help inform the Jurisdictional Steering Committee as they periodically update the evolving S&T plan for the jurisdiction.

requirements.text: All multi-year grant Principal Investigators must submit annual project reports to the cognizant Program Officer no later than 90 days prior to the end of the current budget period, unless a specific program requires more frequent reporting.
requirements.source_quote: For all multi-year grants (including both standard and continuing grants), the Principal Investigator must submit an annual project report to the cognizant Program Officer no later than 90 days prior to the end of the current budget period. (Some programs or awards require submission of more frequent project reports).

requirements.text: No later than 120 days after the grant expires, the PI must submit a final annual project report and a project outcomes report for the general public.
requirements.source_quote: No later than 120 days following expiration of a grant, the PI also is required to submit a final annual project report, and a project outcomes report for the general public.

requirements.text: PIs must use NSF's electronic project-reporting system via Research.gov to prepare and submit both annual and final annual project reports.
requirements.source_quote: PIs are required to use NSF's electronic project-reporting system, available through Research.gov, for preparation and submission of annual and final annual project reports.

requirements.text: The submission of a report via Research.gov serves as the PI's certification that the contents are accurate and complete.
requirements.source_quote: Submission of the report via Research.gov constitutes certification by the PI that the contents of the report are accurate and complete.

requirements.text: The project outcomes report, which serves as a brief public summary of the project's nature and outcomes, must be prepared and submitted using Research.gov.
requirements.source_quote: The project outcomes report also must be prepared and submitted using Research.gov. This report serves as a brief summary, prepared specifically for the public, of the nature and outcomes of the project.

requirements.text: Award recipients must include an estimate of remaining unobligated funds at the end of each report period within the “Changes/Problems” section.
requirements.source_quote: Award recipients must include an estimate of remaining unobligated funds at the end of each report period within the “Changes/Problems” section

requirements.text: If the estimated remaining unobligated funds are greater than 20% of the current year award amount, the PI must provide a plan and timeline for expenditure of those funds in the annual and final annual project report.
requirements.source_quote: If that estimate is greater than 20% of the current year award amount, the PI also must provide a plan and timeline for expenditure of those funds in the annual and final annual project report.

requirements.text: E-CORE recipients are required to participate in the EDOCS data-collection activity coordinated by NSF EPSCoR.
requirements.source_quote: E-CORE recipients will be required to participate in the EDOCS data-collection activity coordinated by NSF EPSCoR and carried out by its designated entity.

cap_usd.quote: Funding requests must be for a duration of four (4) years, with a maximum budget of up to $10 million total.

max_years.quote: Funding requests must be for a duration of four (4) years

cost_share.quote: "Committed cost sharing is not allowed for the new E-CORE awards; however, cost share is required for the E-CORE four-year renewal project awards"

subaward_mtdc_limit_usd.quote: 2 CFR 200.1: MTDC includes "up to the first $50,000 of each subaward".

equipment_threshold_usd.quote: revised to increase the equipment threshold from $5,000 to $10,000 to align with updates provided in Title 2 CFR § 200.

letters_of_support.quote: "Letters of support are not allowed ... However, up to ten letters of collaboration (two pages or fewer) from partners or jurisdictional officials may be included"
